newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki up, but off highs in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki up, but off highs in heavy volume.

text.p: Shares joined a Europe-wide rally on Wednesday, but even though they ended off their best and failed to match last week's all-time peaks, operators said they saw no reason for the uptrend to falter.

The FOX index rose 1.27 percent to 1,202.43, some 24 points shy of its all-time best of 1,226.84 on July 17 and short of a its session high. The all-share HEX gained 1.1 percent to 3,469.10 points. Volume was massive at above 900 million markka.
"We'll continue to take our direction from Wall Street, but there's no reason this should easily turn down," one market analyst said, after the U.S. market opened higher.

Brokers said that with many markets in truly bullish mood, Helsinki could have gone higher if it had not been for hesitance around bellwether Nokia on the eve of a six-month earnings report from its Swedish rival Ericsson.

"If Ericsson's report is O.K., nothing will upset this market," one broker said. Analysts expect a 21 percent H1 year-on-year pre-tax profit gain from Ericsson to around 5.11 billion crowns when it reports before 0900 GMT on Thursday.
Nokia still managed to join blue-chips leading gains, closing up 2.00 markka at 425.00, off an intraday high of 429.50 in hefty 380 million markka trade.
Merita gained sharply in heavy volume as overseas investors remained enthusiastic on the share, brokers said.

It closed up 1.30 markka at 23.30 after touching an all-time high 23.40. Brokers said Merita was boosted by hopes for bumper gains from the stocks rally, but also by market talk it was considering a share issue to pay down its debt to the state. A Merita spokesman said the talk was unfounded.
UPM-Kymmene led forestries higher, gaining 1.90 markka to 133.50, while Enso added 1.10 to close at 49.30.
Raisio rose 5.00 markka to 610.00, as brokers saw signs it was stabilising in the low 600s after last week's surge.
